rubrics.rubric: Do the quotation and memo use the required artifacts, and does the workbook have complete source-grounded structure and pricing?
criterion: The workbook uses the exact required filename.
The memo is a readable DOCX named exactly Internal_Memo_Clearwater_Product_Selection.docx.
The workbook contains the five instructed tabs in the instructed order.

The Cover Page includes the quote number, quotation date, RFQ reference, SentinelGas Technologies name and any source-provided company details, full RFQ customer details, 60-day validity, and Net 30 terms; unavailable vendor contact details are not invented.
The Bill of Materials covers all five plant areas and all 38 detection points.
Each detector line includes the instructed identification, range, quantity, list-price, discount, and net-price fields.
Detector and controller discounts follow the applicable Government/Municipal schedules in the price list.
Area subtotals and the grand total reconcile to the line items.
The controller and panel configuration is included in the BOM.

rubrics.rubric: Does memo section (a) make a complete and defensible Area 3 H2S selection between H2S-200 and H2S-300X?
criterion: The memo compares H2S-200 and H2S-300X on detection range.
The memo compares sensor life, IP rating, certifications, diagnostics or features, detector price, and replacement-sensor price.
The memo calculates a transparent five-year cost for the Area 3 quantity using a consistent stated pricing basis.
The memo recognizes the RFQ's Area 3 range and the manager's premium-model guidance.
The recommendation explains the effect of the confined-space application.
Any wider-than-requested range is flagged as a deviation and justified rather than described as exact range compliance.
The final recommendation is consistent with the BOM and compliance matrix.

rubrics.rubric: Does the proposed controller configuration meet the RFQ spare-capacity requirement with correct arithmetic and comparison?
criterion: Total controller channels, used channels, and spare channels are shown.
Spare capacity is calculated as spare channels divided by total channels.
The recommended configuration is correctly compared with the RFQ's minimum 20% spare capacity.
The CP-32 plus EXP-16 price is calculated from the supplied price list and applicable controller discount.
The CP-64 alternative is priced and its spare capacity is calculated.
The memo explains the cost and capacity tradeoff between the two configurations.

rubrics.rubric: Does the five-year TCO tab provide a correct per-area comparison for SentinelGas, MSA, Honeywell, and the Rosemount IR substitute where applicable?
criterion: The comparison is broken out by plant area.
Year 1 equipment cost is separated from Years 2 through 5 sensor-replacement costs.
Replacement counts use ceil(60 divided by sensor life in months) minus 1.
SentinelGas replacement counts and costs use the selected models' source data.
MSA and Honeywell sensor lives and replacement assumptions are tied to cited manufacturer information.
Rosemount 625IR is used for the IR combustible alternative where applicable.
Unavailable competitor lifespan or replacement-price data are labeled as data gaps rather than invented.
The instructed SentinelGas proxy is used only for unavailable competitor replacement-sensor prices and is stated explicitly.

Competitor Year 1 detector pricing uses a cited public price or quote; if no reliable price is available, the analysis labels the data gap and any documented estimate or range rather than silently extending the replacement-sensor proxy.
Area and solution totals reconcile to their component calculations.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Technical Compliance Matrix evaluate every RFQ requirement accurately across the proposed and competitor products?
criterion: The matrix includes one row for each material RFQ specification, including per-area detection ranges.
The matrix separately presents SentinelGas, MSA S5000, Sensepoint XCD, and Rosemount 625IR specifications where applicable.

Applicable comparison cells use only Compliant, Partially Compliant, Non-Compliant, or Not Specified; product/specification combinations outside the product's intended gas application are explicitly marked N/A rather than misclassified as a documentation gap.
Each stated product specification names its source.
Detection-range deviations are flagged and explained.
Communication-protocol claims distinguish 4-20 mA, Modbus, HART, and other documented capabilities accurately.
Operating-temperature compliance uses the applicable sensor limits rather than relying only on a broader housing certification range.
Ingress protection and hazardous-area approvals are compared accurately.
SIL claims preserve the source wording and distinguish certification, suitability, optional availability, and absence of published information.
Sensor-life comparisons identify missing information as a data gap.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Spare Parts & Stocking tab calculate five-year replacement demand, on-site stock, and discounted pricing correctly?
criterion: Each replacement sensor needed by the selected detector mix is listed.
Installed quantity and sensor life match the selected models.
Replacements per unit use the instructed 60-month formula.
Total replacement quantity reconciles to installed quantity and replacements per unit.
Recommended on-site stock is stated for each applicable replacement part.
Replacement-sensor pricing applies the Government/Municipal discount.
Zero scheduled replacement is shown where the documented life spans the full five-year period.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo reconcile all other RFQ-versus-briefing deviations and remain consistent with the quotation?
criterion: Memo section (c) compares each selected detector's range with the RFQ range for every plant area.
Memo section (c) compares the selections with the manager's standard-versus-premium guidance.
The Area 4 H2S selection explicitly resolves the conflict between the RFQ range and any standard-series recommendation.
Every material deviation is identified in both the memo and compliance matrix.
The memo distinguishes requirements from preferred features and sales differentiators.
The memo, BOM, TCO, compliance matrix, and spare-parts tab use a consistent selected product mix.
Unsupported competitor facts are not presented as established specifications.
